title: Listo Pairing Ledger
lede: Every subclass in the modlist, swept for its best twenty-level expression, scored on ten axes across three acts, and paired with every other. The entries are the Pareto frontier over the four blocks; the field table is the audit trail.
footer: Swept and scored 19 August 2026 against the installed Listonomicon 10.2 paks. 157 subclasses enumerated, 150 chassis scored, 11,175 pairings computed. Every number on this page is derived at render time; none is hand-written.

Quiver.note: A bow Fighter whose Arcane Arrows are slot-free, concentration-free single-target removal on a short-rest clock — ten arrows and five shot types by Act II. It buys that with no area answer at all, no outward rescue, and a shieldless armour profile.

Banner.note: The Fighter that spends its Action Surge on the other body: Inspiring Surge at 10 converts every surge into the partner's reaction attack, and Rallying Cry makes Second Wind an outward heal from level 3. Zero control and zero area damage in exchange.

Riposte.note: The only Fighter whose whole kit rides the short-rest clock: six superiority dice recharging every short rest, a d10 manoeuvre rider on three attacks per Action by 11, and Riposte spending Lone Wolf's spare reaction. Trip Attack is its only control and it is pure save-DC.

Bastion.note: The save chassis. Brutish Durability at Fighter 7 is an unconditional, resource-free +1d6 on every saving throw, stacked on heavy armour, a shield and Heavy Armour Master; Brute Force adds a free rider to every hit. It does nothing at all to a crowd and nothing at all for the partner.

Bulwark.note: The dedicated protector: Warding Maneuver is reaction prevention aimed at whoever is next to you, and Unwavering Mark forcibly redirects a marked enemy's attacks onto the armoured half. Its rescue only reaches 1.5m, which is the wrong range for a caster partner.

Keen.note: Champion's 18–20 crit range and a free attack-roll reroll every turn, with the rider Champion structurally lacks bought from a three-level Blood Hunter dip — Crimson Rite is at-will and costs no clock. Four short-rest Blood Curses are its only control.

Tempo.note: The only chassis in the list that literally hands the partner an Action: Borrowed Time, 18m, off a small Intelligence-scaled long-rest pool, at the cost of a halved following turn — and it cannot be combined with Action Surge on the same turn. Alacrity stacks a third reaction on Lone Wolf's two.

Echo.note: A second, flying, 1-HP body that threatens its own zone and lets Unleash Incarnation add a melee attack per Attack action taken — so Action Surge becomes attacks rather than just an Action. Thief's extra bonus action pays the swap costs. Legion of One is not implemented, so 18–20 is dead subclass space.

Warmage.note: The Fighter that converts Action Surge into casting: War Magic at 5 swaps an attack for a cantrip, Improved War Magic at 12 swaps two for a levelled spell, and the surge resets the counter — so one turn is attacks plus cantrip then spell plus attack. The full Wizard list buys Shield, Haste and a thin control suite, all off a small slot pool.

Kinesis.note: Protective Field spends a psionic die to cut damage on the partner from 9m, on their turn, off a pool that scales to twelve dice and partly refreshes on a short rest. Psionic Strike's rider is Force, which is the least-resisted type under Absolute Wrath. It has no area answer whatsoever.

Wyrmling.note: A dragon that shares your initiative and acts without being commanded, plus Rallying Surge turning every Action Surge into the partner's reaction attack. The largest raw action-economy Fighter on paper, carried by custom Osiris scripting the author warns needs a fresh playthrough.

Sigil.note: The widest toolbox in the class and almost all of it short-rest: Hill Rune's physical resistance under heavy armour and a shield, Storm Rune's disadvantage reactions that never decay, Runic Shield forcing a reroll on a hit aimed at the partner, and from 15 every rune fires twice per short rest. Sleight of Hand at 3 quietly opens the Act II and Act III pickpocket gates.

Resolve.note: Elegant Courtier at Fighter 7 is a third saving-throw proficiency, a source this run otherwise restricts to the level-1 class, Lone Wolf and Resilient — so the Samurai reaches four disjoint saves covering Wis, Con and Dex inside Act I without spending a feat. Fighting Spirit buys advantage plus temp HP three times a rest; the subclass offers no control and nothing outward.

Bullseye.note: Four attacks per Action by 20, a level-scaled Steady Aim rider on every one of them, and Rapid Strike's bonus-action attack — the cleanest single-target ladder in the class, and Steady Aim recharges on a short rest. No area damage, no control, nothing for the partner, and no shield behind the bow.

Hadar.note: Hunger of Hadar, Fear and Evard's arrive free of the known list and, from Sorcerer 6, cast off sorcery points with no verbal or somatic components — so the area-denial engine runs on a second resource and works while Silenced. Psychic resistance plus advantage on Charm and Fright saves patches the two conditions a duo cannot break. It is a d6 body in a robe with nothing aimed at its partner.

Affinity.note: Amethyst ancestry adds Charisma to every Magic Missile dart, in Force — the type almost nothing in Absolute Wrath's resistance layers touches — and Quickened plus Action Surge plus Lone Wolf's second Action stack four casts into a round. The highest single-target floor in the list, paid for out of a long-rest slot pool on a body with AC 13 and a d6 hit die.

Chosen.note: A Cleric domain's whole list becomes Sorcerer spells at level 1 — off Charisma, Metamagic-eligible, free of the known list — so Twinned Haste covers a two-person party outright and Twinned Death Ward, Revivify and Greater Restoration cover it again. Medium armour and shields at level 1 and Extra Attack at 6 fix the class's two structural holes. It is not a damage chassis and never becomes one.

Anointed.note: Extra Attack at Sorcerer 6 and Divine Smite fed by a full caster's slot table, under Aura of Protection once the Paladin block lands around character 12. Six Paladin levels bought after the fact cost the heavy armour and the Wis/Cha saves, and the 14/6 split costs a feat outright.

Umbral.note: Hound of Ill Omen is disadvantage on a target's saves off a short-rest recharge — it costs no concentration, so it never competes with the partner's one spell, and unlike a save DC it does not decay as enemy saves inflate. Strength of the Grave at level 1 is a flat refusal to go down, and Umbral Form at 18 is resistance to everything but Force and Radiant for ten turns.

Gale.note: Tempest Cleric 1 buys heavy armour and martial weapons for a d6 caster and Channel Divinity at 2 maximises every lightning and thunder damage roll twice per short rest, with Heart of the Storm adding free splash on every such cast and Action Surge repeating it. Everything it does is one commonly-resisted damage type, with no strip, and the three-class split costs a feat.

Luck.note: Bend Luck spends Lone Wolf's spare reaction on a plus-or-minus d4 against any visible creature's attack roll, check or save — a single-roll intervention on the enemy save that must fail or the partner save that must not. Fighter 1 first buys heavy armour and a shield onto a d6 body. The surge table itself is a liability in a party where either character going down ends the fight.

Dread.note: Conquering Presence frightens every enemy in 30 feet off a short-rest Channel Oath and spends no concentration at all, so the partner keeps the pair's other spell slot; Aura of Conquest then bills every frightened creature half your Paladin level in psychic each turn. It is a Wisdom-save engine, and Wisdom DCs are exactly what Combat Extender inflates.

Devout.note: The plain pick, and the plain pick is a good pick here: Aura of Protection puts Charisma on both characters' saves from level 6 and Aura of Devotion makes both charm-immune at 7, in a run whose rebuilt enemy casters open with charm. It brings no control, no area damage and no clock of its own.

Enmity.note: Vow of Enmity is blanket advantage on one target off a short-rest charge, and six Warlock levels feed two third-level pact slots per short rest straight into Divine Smite. The class file's own arithmetic says this trade loses: Paladin 17 / Warlock 3 holds more units per long-rest cycle than Paladin 13 / Warlock 7 does.

Warding.note: Aura of Warding at 7 gives both characters resistance to spell damage at 9m — the damage type the run's rebuilt enemy casters lean on hardest — stacked on Aura of Protection at 6 and heavy armour with a shield. A level 7 Ancients paladin is carrying the other character's survivability, and almost nothing else.

Bleak.note: Black Flames stacks 2d10 fire plus 2d10 necrotic and a Sickened debuff onto a smite the same turn, the level 7 aura widens the crit range for both characters, and Expertise in Intimidation at level 1 clears the Hag's Hair gate outright. Five Sorcerer levels buy Quickened, Twinned and third-level slots to smite from.

Regent.note: Champion Challenge pulls a group's attacks onto the armoured half off a short-rest Channel Oath, which is the only taunt shape a duo can use, and Aura of Vitality turns a bonus action into repeatable outward healing from Paladin 9. Divine Allegiance and Warding Bond are redirection, and in a two-body party redirection just moves damage from one half to the other.

Lunar.note: The most duo-shaped oath in the class: Divine Guardian halves all incoming damage on the partner for ten turns off a short-rest Channel Oath, Aura of Moonlight subtracts Charisma from every hit either character takes, and Full Moon blinds and slows a 9m group as a bonus action from level 1. The whole kit competes for one Channel Oath charge.

Spite.note: Unholy Smite replaces Divine Smite outright, so every point of smite damage is necrotic — a straight downgrade against the shadow-cursed and undead of Act 2, and an upgrade against very little. Aura of Hate buffs only fiends and undead, so a normal partner receives nothing from the level 7 aura at all.

Squall.note: Storm Shift is three times Druid level in temporary hit points — sixty at 20 — lasting all day for one Wild Shape charge, with Wisdom added to every Lightning, Thunder and Cold damage roll on top. From level 10 the same buff turns enemy elemental immunity into resistance, which is the answer to the one problem an elemental caster has in a party too small to carry a second damage type.

Ember.note: The Wildfire Spirit is a permanent extra body that also casts your spells from its own position — a second point of origin for area damage, which a two-person party otherwise cannot generate — and Blazing Revival is an automatic second life. Revivify arrives on the Druid list at 5, which no other circle here manages.

Rime.note: From level 10 every Cold spell knocks its failed saves Prone and spends no concentration doing it, so the area control rides damage you were casting anyway. Winter Spirit is five times Druid level in temp HP plus Wisdom added to every damaging Druid spell — not only the cold ones. Everything offensive is Cold, with no strip, which is the risk.

Aspect.note: Four aspects across fire/radiant, lightning/thunder, cold/piercing and force/bludgeoning, each giving a scaling cantrip and a revelation spell once per Wild Shape — so the damage is at-will, needs no concentration, and can always pick a type Absolute Wrath's resistance layers do not cover, including Force. The whole thing runs on the short-rest Wild Shape clock.

Wellspring.note: Natural Recovery is the class's only in-day slot refund, and it lands on a short rest — which matters more than usual when a long rest costs 120 supplies and camp cost is 3. What it buys is a longer day, not a better round: the weakest circle for action economy, adding no bodies of its own beyond what every Druid already has.

Wildform.note: Wild Shape is a second hit-point bar the overhaul keeps Action Surge, feats and multiclass features working inside, refreshed twice per short rest — six bars a long-rest cycle. It does not add a body; it makes the one body very hard to remove, and the beast damage never scales into Act III.

Tide.note: Wrath of the Sea turns a spare Bonus Action into Wisdom-scaled cold damage and a five-metre push, every turn, for no resource beyond the Wild Shape charge that started it — and Lone Wolf's second bonus action buys two of them. Oceanic Gift at 14 projects the whole engine onto the partner for one more charge.

Pack.note: Every Spirit Totem is an aura pointed at the other character — Bear's temp HP equal to 5 plus Druid level, Flumph making every heal you cast heal the whole aura again, Hawk handing the partner advantage off a reaction — and Mighty Summoner scales Conjure Animals, Find Familiar and Flock of Familiars into a genuine second front. This is the closest a two-person party gets to a four-person one.

Symbiote.note: A real Extra Attack outside Wild Shape, Shillelagh putting Wisdom on attack and damage, Symbiotic Entity adding 1d6 to every hit and four times Druid level in temp HP, and a Halo of Spores reaction on top — with Dealer's Choice letting Acid, Necrotic and Poison be picked independently to dodge whatever is resisted. Cleric first buys heavy armour and Wis/Cha saves.

Omen.note: Star Druid Tweaks moves Cosmic Omen onto the short-rest clock, so a plus-or-minus d6 on the partner's saving throws is insurance you can actually afford to spend three or four times a rest cycle. Chalice doubles every slot-cast heal, Archer turns the spare bonus action into radiant damage every turn, and Dragon form keeps the pair's one concentration spell up.

Dawnrite.note: Crimson Rite is at-will damage on no clock at all, Brand of Sundering doubles its dice against the branded target from 11, and Rite Revival at 18 turns the first drop to 0 HP into 1 HP instead. Curse Specialist front-loads a fourth Blood Maledict from level 3, and the Exorcist curse at 15 is a duo's only reliable Charm and Fear break. It has no area damage whatsoever and cannot clear a single named skill gate.

Hybrid.note: Extra Attack, a Crimson Rite rider on every hit including the fists, and a bonus-action unarmed strike that Lone Wolf's second bonus action doubles — the highest raw single-target ladder in the Order list, reached without spending a feat. Bloodlust is the price: below half HP a failed Wisdom save turns this body on its partner, and it triggers exactly when the fight is already going badly.

Mutagen.note: Potency and Celerity are up to five raw ability points past the cap Listo removed, for the cost of a short rest, and Precision widens the crit range while Cruelty buys an extra attack after every attack. Every resistance mutagen hands out a matching vulnerability, and Cruelty's price is disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saves — which is the half of the save table that loses fights.

Scarbrand.note: Brand of the Sapping Scar at 11 is blanket Disadvantage on the branded creature's saving throws, delivered by a free interrupt, costing no concentration and no slot — so it never competes with the partner's one spell and, unlike a save DC, it does not decay as Combat Extender inflates enemy saves. Pact Magic off Intelligence on short-rest slots pays for the control, but the spell ceiling is level 4 forever.

Abjurer.note: The only Cleric with native Counterspell, holding it on Lone Wolf's spare reaction, plus Arcane Abjuration's level-gated banish on a short-rest charge. Gives up armour, weapons and any damage engine beyond a Potent-Spellcasting cantrip.

Thrall.note: Control Undead converts an enemy into a third body on a short-rest Channel Divinity charge — the one thing a duo is structurally short of. Pays for it with no heavy armour, no Extra Attack and a necrotic Divine Strike that Absolute Wrath resists.

Torpor.note: Deep Slumber strips an enemy to one action with no reactions, and Inception's disadvantage on the first save does not decay as enemy DCs climb. No armour past medium, no martial weapons, and no damage worth the name.

Prophecy.note: Prophecy of Doom is slot-free, concentration-free area control on a short-rest charge, and the free swappable skill proficiency quietly covers gates. Discounted a rung throughout because the effect table is random and cannot be planned around.

Anvil.note: Heavy armour, shield, Soul of the Forge's +1 AC and fire resistance, then non-magical physical resistance at 17, all stacking under Heavy Armour Master and Lone Wolf's halving. Buys that with essentially no damage: simple weapons, no Extra Attack, a fire-locked Divine Strike.

Sentinel.note: Sentinel at Death's Door turns a critical hit on either character into a normal one, deleting the duo's usual failure mode off a reaction Lone Wolf gives away spare. No armour past medium, no weapons, and Path to the Grave is your partner's damage, not yours.

Witchhunter.note: Spell Shield hands the partner temp HP, spell resistance and advantage on spell saves for one Channel Divinity charge, and Rebuke Invoker sinks the spare reaction. Heavy armour and martial weapons, but no Extra Attack, so the force damage never becomes a real single-target engine.

Lorekeeper.note: Double proficiency in two knowledge skills plus Bard Expertise, Jack of All Trades and Guidance covers nearly every campaign gate, and Divine Foreknowledge is an hour of advantage on everything at 17. Neither half contributes damage.

Vitalist.note: Disciple of Life on every heal, Preserve Life on a short-rest charge, Revivify, Death Ward and Supreme Healing at 17 make it the duo's insurance against losing either character. Heavy armour but no martial weapons and no Extra Attack — it is a medic, not a body.

Flare.note: Improved Warding Flare imposes disadvantage on attacks against your partner, and Lone Wolf's spare reaction lets it fire twice a round; Radiance of the Dawn is a genuine short-rest repeatable AoE. No armour or weapons beyond the base class.

Thornclad.note: The only domain with built-in Shillelagh, so a heavy-armoured Wisdom melee body needs no feat tax and can spend its feats on Heavy Armour Master instead. Divine Strike is the only rider, and there is no Extra Attack behind it.

Nightward.note: Invocation of Night blinds everything within 9m for Cleric-level rounds off a short-rest charge with no concentration and no slot, and Ward of Shadows covers the partner from Cleric 6. No armour or weapons beyond the base class.

Authority.note: Voice of Authority buys your partner a free weapon attack from every buff or heal you put on them, at no resource cost, from level 1 — the cleanest structural fix in the file for a two-body economy. Embodiment of the Law bonus-actions enchantments on top. No Extra Attack of its own.

Bond.note: Emboldening Bond is a permanent d4 on both characters' attacks, checks and saves, and Sanctuary plus Balm of Peace give the partner prevention and a short-rest heal. Protective Bond only moves damage from one half of the party to the other, and the domain grants no armour past medium.

Titan.note: The only Cleric domain with Haste on its own list, handing the partner an extra Action from caster 5, plus Avatar of Battle's physical resistance and Feat of Strength's flat +10. Heavy armour but no martial weapons and no Extra Attack, so it hastes rather than hits.

Stormvest.note: A one-level Tempest dip buys heavy armour, shields and martial weapons so Charisma metamagic can Twin Haste onto both bodies, with Destructive Wrath maximising lightning off a short-rest charge. Long-rest slots and a small sorcery-point pool are the whole fuel supply.

Stormcall.note: Heavy armour and martial weapons on a body that maximises lightning and thunder through Destructive Wrath twice a short rest, with Wrath of the Storm sinking reactions. Locked to two commonly resisted damage types and with no Extra Attack behind them.

Duplicity.note: Invoke Duplicity is one decoy until the level-17 upgrade to four, and the domain grants no armour, no weapons and a poison Divine Strike that almost everything resists. The weakest vanilla chassis in the file, and the Listo buff mod the docs recommend is not installed.

Sanctuary.note: Twilight Sanctuary temp-HPs or cleanses charm and fear on both bodies every round for one Channel Divinity charge a short rest refunds, alongside Revivify, Death Ward and Aura of Life. Heavy armour and martial weapons but no Extra Attack, so the damage never leaves the floor.

Warpriest.note: The only domain with true Extra Attack at 6, plus a War Priest bonus-action swing and Action Surge as a third Action — the highest raw swing count a Cleric can reach. It never gets Improved Extra Attack, so the ceiling stops at Act II's fourth rung.

Pyre.note: Heavy armour, martial weapons, a Priest of Zeal bonus-action swing from level 1, Fighter's Extra Attack and Action Surge, with Consuming Fervor maximising Fireball twice a short rest. The Cleric half arrives late, so Revivify and Death Ward do not land until Act II.

Legerdemain.note: Four Expertise, Reliable Talent and a permanent invisible Mage Hand, with the Wizard dip turning Listo's scroll drops into a real library. Nothing aimed at the partner at all, and Int competes with Dex for the whole run.

Alacrity.note: Gloom Stalker's initiative and first-round attack feed Assassin's restored Action, guaranteed crits on the surprised and advantage on anything yet to act. All of it front-loads: against long fights with reinforcements it contributes least when the duo is most at risk.

Sightline.note: Insightful Fighting is a repeatable no-ally Sneak Attack enabler with no rest clock, and Steady Eye plus Reliable Talent plus Expertise covers every search gate for the whole campaign. No area answer of any kind and nothing aimed at the partner.

Tactician.note: Bonus-action Help lifts a downed partner or hands them advantage without spending an Action, and the Bard dip stacks Expertise for the face. Misdirection's redirect only ever points at your partner, which in a duo is the wrong direction.

Wail.note: Wails from the Grave splits Sneak Attack across two targets on a kill-fed Soul Trinket economy rather than a rest clock, and Whispers of the Dead grants every skill of one ability once per short rest. Death's Friend at 17 finally makes both targets take full damage.

Skirmish.note: Ambush Master's +5 initiative and party-wide advantage mark help both characters, and Survivalist hands over two free Expertise. The subclass adds no damage of its own before Sudden Strike at 17, so the first two acts are a plain Rogue.

Parry.note: Auspicious Parry turns an incoming hit into 1 damage and Lone Wolf's extra reaction lets you parry and Uncanny Dodge the same round, while Spell Siphon and Disrupt give a duo the enemy-caster answer it otherwise lacks. Costs Intelligence on top of Dexterity, a free off-hand and any shield.

Psiblade.note: Self-sufficient blades, accuracy, mobility and invisibility all out of one die pool, needing no gear and no ally, with Rend Mind the only hard stun on any Rogue here. Psychic is commonly resisted in the late game and the dice economy is the one thing the source could not verify.

Rakish.note: Rakish Audacity gives Sneak Attack with no ally needed, and Paladin buys Extra Attack, Aura of Protection and smites off the same Charisma. Swashbuckler gets nothing from 13 to 20 and the build is genuinely three-stat: Dexterity to hit, Charisma for the aura and Dirty Tricks, Constitution to stay up.

Fasthands.note: Fast Hands, Lone Wolf and Action Surge stack into three bonus actions and three Actions, and Thief's Reflexes adds a whole first round at 17. Nothing aimed at the partner and no area answer, and the author warns Thief's Reflexes misbehaves with shared turns — which is the situation a two-player party is permanently in.

Pirouette.note: Unarmed damage rides the Inspiration die to d12 and Agile Strikes gives a free kick every time you inspire your partner, while Monk supplies Martial Arts and unarmoured AC the College never gets. It never gets Extra Attack, and the AC wants Wisdom on top of Dexterity and Charisma.

Silver.note: Unsettling Words subtracts a visible die from the next save — you see the number before committing the control spell — and Unfailing Inspiration refunds every die that fails. Light armour, no weapon engine, and Silver Tongue may simply not work.

Mantle.note: Mantle of Inspiration is repeatable outward temp HP off the Inspiration clock, which moves to short rest at Bard 5. The real defence, Unbreakable Majesty, does not arrive until 14, so the first two acts are a plain Bard in light armour.

Peerless.note: Six proficiencies, Expertise four times, Jack of All Trades and a dialogue-usable Peerless Skill clear every named gate, and Magical Secrets at Bard 6 buys Haste and Revivify four levels early. Light armour and no damage engine at all.

Aria.note: Electrifying Aria repeats for ten turns and degrades enemy Constitution saves each turn instead of decaying, then Finale stuns everything still Electrified — one Action buying a fight's worth of control. Nothing before Bard 14 matches it, and lightning and thunder are the two types Absolute Wrath most reliably resists.

Flourish.note: Extra Attack at 6 with a Flourish rider on each swing, and Goon's interrupt Flourishes turn Lone Wolf's spare reactions into damage; Master's Flourish at 14 makes the rider free. Medium armour and no shield, and the weapon wants Dexterity while the spell DC wants Charisma.

Pathos.note: Poetry in Misery and Tale of Hubris both fire off-turn on Lone Wolf's spare reaction, and Impending Misfortune's flat +10 clears skill gates outright. Nimbus of Pathos ends by dropping its target to 0 HP, which in a duo is half the action economy — it is a nuke you cannot safely aim at your partner.

Anthem.note: Shields and martial weapons on a Charisma caster from the College itself, Extra Attack at 6, Battle Magic's bonus-action attack at 14 and Action Surge as a third Action. It never reaches Improved Extra Attack, so the swing count stops where Act II's ceiling starts.

Rally.note: Banners count as attacks so they cost no tempo after Extra Attack, Red Banner buys your partner a reaction attack, level 6 moves the charges to short rest and Legendary Banner at 17 hands an ally a free attack every turn. No area answer whatsoever.

Cinder.note: Searing Blade strips all resistances and Supernatural Dampening then blocks healing and treats the target as sunlit, so the partner's damage type stops mattering. Its own damage is fire-locked and therefore capped at four from Act II, and it has no area answer.

Ironwill.note: Heavy armour, shield, Heavy Armour Master, Sheer Will's flat reduction and Training From Hell's physical resistance all stack under Lone Wolf's halving, and Sheer Will keeps temporary HP up permanently — which is exactly the condition the Tharchiate Codex blessing checks. Innate Mastery is the only damage the subclass adds.

Oberon.note: A crit threshold reduced by up to 3 feeds Fairy's Curse, which strips an enemy's bonus actions and reactions with no concentration cost, and Shifting Court's position swap pulls the partner out of a pack onto the armoured body. Fairy's Curse does not arrive until Paragon 9, so Act I is a plain armoured swinger.

Armament.note: Scholar's Armament makes Charisma the attack and damage stat, and six Spell Sword Focuses by 17 cover every damage type Absolute Wrath resists — the only genuinely single-stat body in the file. Will Over Weave at 13 is slot-free Counterspell on a short-rest die, and nothing here costs a spell slot because there are none.

Pactblade.note: Short-rest pact slots and Agonizing Blast on a Charisma melee body, with Scholar's Armament putting Charisma on the weapon and Pact of the Blade supplying Extra Attack at Warlock 5. Nothing aimed at the partner, and the Spellblade dip stops five levels short of the feature the plan was named for.

Nirvana.note: Falling Rain is a free-action attack riding every Willpower Die spent, so Lone Wolf's second Action multiplies into more free swings, and Beyond All Limits at 18 refills the pool every turn. No area answer, nothing outward, and the level-17 finisher wants the entire dice pool at once.

Glamour.note: Fey Presence is short-rest area charm-or-fear with no concentration and no slot, available from level 1, and Chains of Carceri adds slot-free Hold Monster later. Expansion gives Archfey no level-14 feature, so the back half of the patron is empty, and there is nothing aimed at the partner at all.

Radiance.note: A bonus-action heal that spends no slot, plus Revivify and Lesser Restoration on short-rest pact slots — the only Charisma blaster in the file that is also the duo's medic. Healing Light's pool is on the long-rest clock, so it is a per-day budget rather than a per-fight one.

Infernal.note: Agonizing Blast is at-will Force damage on no clock, and Dark One's Own Luck, Dark One's Blessing and Fiendish Resilience keep the squishy half of a duo standing. Eldritch Cone carries the crowd answer through Act II and then stops scaling, which is why the area damage falls in Act III.

Whisper.note: Agonizing Blast is unbounded at-will damage, and its many attack rolls make Mortal Reminder's crit-triggered fear fire far more often than the description implies — repeatable single-target control that spends no concentration. Create Thrall at 14 is the only extra body, and there is nothing aimed at the partner.

Blackblade.note: Hex Warrior puts Charisma on the weapon at level one without waiting for Pact of the Blade, and Paladin 8 adds Extra Attack, Aura of Protection and smites fuelled by short-rest pact slots. The split lands off the feat cadence and costs a feat outright, and Paladin taken later grants no heavy armour.

Accursed.note: Hexblade's Curse and Quickened blasts off short-rest pact slots make at-will damage the whole turn, with Twinned metamagic covering both bodies on any single-target buff. Three sorcery points is the whole fuel supply, so Quickened is roughly once per long rest, not a routine.

Warp.note: Warp detonations turn every Eldritch Blast beam into a 3m Force burst — real repeatable AoE on no clock — but Perils of the Warp drains maximum HP on every blast until Gellar's Field arrives at 10, and a two-body party has no third character to cover a caster who is bleeding max HP.

Frenzy.note: Barbarian opener for Str+Con saves, Frenzied Strike as a bonus-action swing, and a Fighter 3 block for Action Surge. Everything distinctive waits for Retaliation at Barbarian 14, so the middle of the run is a plain raging body with no crowd answer at all.

Wildsurge.note: A rage chassis whose output is a random table. Bolstering Magic hands the partner a spell slot or a d3 every rest cycle and Magic Awareness adds proficiency bonus to both characters' saves against spells, but the body itself does nothing a plain Barbarian does not.

Hurl.note: The throwing line: Reckless advantage on thrown attacks, Rage throw damage scaling to +8 at 16, Brutal Critical on thrown crits and Elemental Cleaver supplying a second damage type. Huge size at 14 fixes reach; the crowd answer never arrives.

Totem.note: Bear Heart resistance to everything but psychic under Rage, stacked on Lone Wolf's halving, and Bear Attunement at 14 is a real taunt that pulls fire off the partner. Several Aspect-of-the-Beast options are still buggy in this build.

Null.note: The anti-caster body: Advantage on every spell save while raging, a reaction counterspell resolved on a Constitution check rather than an enemy save, and 2d6 back on every spell save passed. No area answer whatsoever.

Ancestor.note: Spirit Shield spends Lone Wolf's spare Reaction to cut 2d6 rising to 4d6 off the partner, and Ancestral Protectors makes the marked creature attack everyone else at disadvantage for half damage. It reduces rather than redirects, so it is not discounted.

Claw.note: Claws add a third attack to every Attack action, so six swings a round with Lone Wolf's two Actions, and Call the Hunt at 14 gives the partner +1d6 per turn for the whole Rage. The price is no shield and no dual wield.

Granite.note: Resolute Stance imposes disadvantage on every attack against you on demand, and Reckless Attack cancels the self-inflicted disadvantage. Thunderous Blows pushes on every hit for no resource and Unstoppable at 14 answers the Stun and Prone lockouts outright.

Galvanic.note: The only Barbarian with real repeatable AoE — Roaring Crash on entering Rage and a once-per-turn Fulgurant Strike splash — plus Ensnared as a speed-0 rider. Every Bonus Action power competes with Rage itself until the free Lightning Step at 10.

Wraith.note: Heavy armour proficiency at 3, physical resistance and a flat −2 on every incoming instance, stacked under Lone Wolf's halving. The cost is total: unhealable for the whole fight, unable to end the rage, and spellcasting off.

Tundra.note: Storm Aura Tundra hands the partner temp HP every single turn for a Bonus Action with no rest cost, scaling to 6 a turn at 20, and Shielding Storm at 10 shares cold resistance across a 10 ft aura both bodies are always inside.

Fury.note: Divine Fury adds 1d6 plus half Barbarian level of radiant to the first hit each turn and scales on Barbarian levels, so the dip goes the other way; Paladin slots convert to smites and Lay on Hands is the only outward healing in the class.

Aegis.note: Wizard at level 1 for Int and Wis, then Fighter 2 immediately for medium armour, shields and Action Surge. Arcane Ward soaks damage one-for-one and Projected Ward spends the spare Lone Wolf Reaction absorbing the partner's; Improved Abjuration recharges it on every short rest.

Bladesong.note: The only full caster that survives standing in melee: light armour, +4 AC and +4 Constitution saves from Bladesong, Extra Attack at 6, and Song of Defence trading slots for flat damage reduction. Bladesong is a long-rest pool of 2 to 4 uses, which is the resource Listo taxes hardest.

Menagerie.note: Two off-list Conjuration picks at 6 reach into the druid summon pool, and Focused Conjuration at 10 makes damage unable to break concentration on them, so the duo's third and fourth bodies stay up. Ultimate Transposition doubles as a button that extracts the partner from a bad spot.

Portent.note: Portent dice spent through Lone Wolf's second reaction replace a boss's saving throw with a guaranteed failure, or an enemy's attack roll with a miss — control that does not decay as enemy save DCs climb. Expert Divination refunds spent dice on short rests.

Charm.note: Hypnotic Gaze locks one creature down and strips its concentration without spending yours, Split Enchantment doubles Hold Person at 10, and Heightened Spell answers Listo's rising enemy saves. The Sorcerer dip also buys Twinned Death Ward, which in a two-body party covers everyone.

Sculpt.note: Two Lone Wolf Actions of Empowered Evocation fireballs, with Sculpt Spells guaranteeing the partner standing inside them takes nothing, and Overchannel at 14 maximising a 1st-to-5th-level burst. It burns slots faster than any other school and has no defensive layer at all.

Pactbook.note: The slot-economy school: Warlock pact slots on a short-rest clock, five or six unrestricted invocations, ritual casts converted into temp HP from 6, and Heart of Darkness refunding slots on kills at 14. Charm and fear immunity at 10 removes a whole class of run-ending effect.

Litany.note: The only Wizard that raises a downed partner. Erudite Remedy heals at 18 m for a bonus action and hands the target a chosen elemental resistance per die spent; Lesser then Greater Restoration, Raise Dead as a ritual at 10, and Warding Rejuvenation at 14 fill the rest.

Mirage.note: The thinnest school in the file. Improved Minor Illusion is a bonus action whose pull Listo's enemy overhaul has largely broken, and Illusory Self is a once-per-rest guaranteed miss on a d6 body. Everything it does well is what any Wizard does.

Legion.note: Animate Dead++ removes the undead cap entirely and moves the free cast to 5, Undead Thralls Fix repairs the extra-corpse grant, and 7th to 9th level slots buy two more bodies each. The most direct answer in the list to two characters against five-body encounters.

Formula.note: Formulaic Attunement makes spells of the attuned damage type ignore resistance to it, which is the cleanest answer in the school list to Absolute Wrath's layered resistances — at the cost of not being able to change attunement in combat. The Spectral Mind is a remote casting position.

Reaper.note: Reaper doubles every necromancy cantrip target and Negative Energy Infusion puts 1d8 rising to 2d8 on every spell-attack hit, so the damage line is at-will with no clock. Inescapable Destruction at 6 strips necrotic resistance; before that the single damage type is exposed. No defensive layer at all.

Stone.note: The Constitution-save Transmuter's Stone is cheap concentration insurance and one of very few cross-character buffs a Wizard can simply hand to the other player. Beyond that the school is Experimental Alchemy and a blue jay.

Deflection.note: The gish caster that is not Bladesinging: a reaction AC and save spike plus Intelligence to initiative, paired with Lone Wolf's spare reaction, and Deflecting Shroud at 14 hitting everything in a radius. Every number on the mod page is images-only.

Panther.note: Expansion moves Companion's Bond to 3 and adds a Panther that uses your proficiency bonus, is proficient in every saving throw, gains ability score improvements when you do, and can Help as a bonus action — which in a duo is a free revive every turn. Bestial Fury at 11, Share Spells at 15.

Valkyrie.note: The highest raw damage ceiling of the conclaves: Valkyrie's landing Extra Attack, Zeal stacking to a second Extra Attack every seven swings, and Divine Flurry's five-attack burst at 11. Herald of the Sun toggles Radiant or Fire, which covers physical resistance; the Faded window afterwards is a real cost with no third body to hide behind.

Drake.note: A drake third body from 3 whose Infused Strikes adds 1d6 of its essence type to any weapon attack by anything within 30 ft that it can see — the partner included. Drake's Breath at 11 is the only AoE, once per long rest or by spending a 3rd-level slot.

Parley.note: Bard at level 1 for three skills and Dex+Cha, then Bard 3 for Expertise twice and Jack of All Trades; Otherworldly Glamour then adds the Ranger's Wisdom modifier to every Charisma check. One body carries the whole campaign's dialogue and lockpicking, and Song of Rest pays part of the long-rest bill.

Ambush.note: Rogue at level 1 for four skills and Expertise twice, then Assassin 3 for a restored Action and Bonus Action at the start of combat, on top of Dread Ambusher's +3 initiative and first-turn extra attack. Iron Mind at Ranger 7 would have patched the Wisdom hole, but Lone Wolf already covers it.

Planar.note: Planar Warrior converts all of an attack's damage to Force and adds 1d8 rising to 2d8, which deletes Absolute Wrath's layered resistances rather than working around them. Distant Strike at 11 teleports between attacks and grants a third attack whenever there are three enemies.

Volley.note: Nothing until 11, then Volley — full weapon damage to every target in range, no save, no resource — fired twice a round on Lone Wolf's second Action, with arrow types covering the resistance spread. Colossus Slayer carries the single-target line and Uncanny Dodge or Evasion arrives at 15.

Quarry.note: Slayer's Prey rides without concentration so it stacks with Hunter's Mark, and Hunter's Sense makes the next hit bypass all resistances and immunities. Magic-User's Nemesis at 11 is a counterspell on a reaction and Slayer's Counter at 15 auto-succeeds the boss's control save.

Warden.note: Guardian form trades movement down to 5 ft for Large size, extended reach, temp HP every turn and +2 max HP per ranger level, and at 15 Guardian Aura heals a hurt partner every turn for no action and no camp supplies. It pairs with a bow, not a charge.

Frostglare.note: Glaring Frost fires a blind off any Cold or Radiant damage, so Paladin smites and radiant arrows both trigger it, and Snowborn Anthelion at 15 spreads the save to everything within 3 m. Snow Blindness turns mass blindness into passive damage on every action an enemy takes.

Swarm.note: Flurry of Moths blinds one target every round after you attack, for no resource, no action and no concentration, and Mighty Swarm at 11 adds a rider and raises the die. The teleport option is a free reposition every round, which is the answer to being focused with no third body to peel.

Zephyr.note: Elemental Strikes replace the default unarmed attack, which also puts the extended range, the chosen element and a push or pull rider on every opportunity attack — control on the enemy's turn for no resource, twice a round with Lone Wolf's second reaction. Damage-type selection answers Absolute Wrath without swapping gear.

Mercy.note: Cleric 1 for Wis+Cha and Life's Disciple of Life, then a deep Monk. From 11 every Flurry strike can be replaced with a free full-power heal on the partner, twice a round on Lone Wolf's two bonus actions, paid for in ki that refills on a short rest — and Hand of Ultimate Mercy at 17 is an in-combat resurrection.

Umbra.note: Rogue at level 1 for four skills and Expertise twice, Thief 3 for a second bonus action on top of Lone Wolf's — three Flurries a round — then a deep Monk. Shadow Arts covers the scouting a two-body party has no room for: Hide, party-wide Pass Without Trace and Shadow Step, all off the ki pool.

Breath.note: Breath of the Dragon replaces one attack of the Attack action, so it costs no bonus action and can be fired from both Lone Wolf Actions, for two Martial Arts dice rising to three at 11 and four at 17. Aspect of the Wyrm at 11 is the only feature in the class that hands the partner a resistance.

Astral.note: The single-stat Monk: Wisdom drives attack, damage, Unarmoured Defence AC and the Ki Save DC, and the arms deal Force, the least-resisted type in the list. Deflect Energy turns each of Lone Wolf's two reactions into 1d10 + Wis of mitigation, and Awakened at 17 makes it three attacks per Action.

Kinship.note: One concentration bond covers the entire party from level 3: temp HP equal to your Wisdom modifier on both characters at the start of every turn with no action, plus a chosen blessing — +1d4 to attacks and saves, or +1 AC and three resistances. Guardian of Light grants shield proficiency, keeps Unarmoured Defence and gives advantage on concentration checks.

Edge.note: Kensei turns Monk into a weapon character, which matters because Listo's weapon pool is enormous and its unarmed pool is not. Agile Parry is +2 AC on nearly every turn for free, Deft Strike adds a Martial Arts die for 1 ki, and Fighter 3 buys Action Surge plus a Fighting Style feat-neutral.

Undying.note: Mastery of Death at 11 converts every death into 1 ki, repeatably, off a pool that refills on a short rest — the strongest single anti-wipe line in the file for a run where losing either body ends the fight. Touch of Death stacks Wis + monk level in temp HP on every kill.

Topple.note: Topple, Push and Stagger ride every Flurry strike off the Ki Save DC — the Wisdom-based DC this build already maximises — costing no concentration and refilling on short rests, and 1411 splits them into First and Second Strike versions so they spread across two targets. Quivering Palm at 17.

Sunbolt.note: The only Monk that fights at range without leaving the class: four Dex-based radiant bolts a turn, six for 1 ki, plus Searing Arc Strike as a bonus-action upcast Burning Hands from 6 and Searing Sunburst at 11. The cost is that it scales on Dexterity, so it gets nothing from the Ki Save DC change and cannot Stun at range.

Panache.note: Superior Defense adds Charisma to unarmoured AC on top of Dexterity, and the Parry stance subtracts 1d20 plus both modifiers from every attack's damage. Extra Attack at 5 and a third reaction at 9 are both gated on holding Panache, which outside crits and kills with a one-handed piercing weapon only returns on a long rest.

Stare.note: An at-will bonus-action Stare that permanently sinks one enemy's saving throws, with Bold Stares riding it for free forever — Blinding, Sundering, then Withering at 11 making a boss pass DC 20 Wisdom or its spell fails outright. The Resistance boon turns Staring into resistance to all damage at 10. No Extra Attack and no area answer at all.

Grace.note: Tricks implanted on the partner fire as free actions when their trigger hits, off a pool of 3 + class level that refreshes on a SHORT rest — 23 of them at 20. Mesmeric Mirror is an automatic miss, Touch Treatment is Lesser then Greater Restoration at 18 m with no trigger, Gift of Will hands the partner +Cha and half level on a Wisdom save, and Compel Alacrity is Haste.

Reagent.note: Artificer 1 opens for Int+Con, medium armour, shields and free Sleight of Hand that becomes Expertise at 6. Six elixirs a rest each carrying 2d6 temp HP, free Lesser Restoration from 9, Death Ward at 13, free Greater Restoration and Heal at 15 and Revivify at 17 — the only subclass that pays for itself in camp supplies.

Plate.note: Arcane Armor supplies heavy armour itself, so the Fighter dip is bought purely for Action Surge, a Fighting Style and Second Wind and loses nothing. Guardian's reaction at 9 makes an attacker save or be yanked 6 m off the partner, and Lone Wolf's second reaction means you keep one in reserve.

Bombard.note: The cannon is built on the Ranger's Companion template, so it resummons without a daily charge — a repeatable Flamethrower cone from level 3. Arcane Firearm adds 1d8 to a damage roll on every spell from 5, Explosive Cannon adds another 1d8 at 9, and Fortified Position at 15 fields two cannons at once, which with a Homunculus is four bodies from one character.

Steelward.note: Intelligence drives attack, damage, spell DC and the number of Arcane Jolt uses, and Enhanced Weapon self-supplies the magical prerequisite. Extra Attack at 5, a Steel Defender whose Deflect Attack imposes disadvantage on anything aimed at the partner, and Arcane Jolt healing 2d6 rising to 4d6 outward off the attack routine for no action.

Armament.name: Armament & Kinship
Armament.tag: single-stat weapon paragon + monk bond support
Armament.verdict: Reads as. The only body in the file that spends no slot at all, bolted to the only support whose entire package is one concentration bond — so the damage, the Counterspell and the party buff all survive a short rest untouched. Six Spell Sword Focuses answer every type Absolute Wrath resists, and the bond's blessing tops up the saves a Charisma-only chassis has no other way to buy.
Armament.cost: Costs. Neither half can pick the other up — there is no revive and no heal anywhere in the pair, and the temp-HP tick is the whole cushion. The crowd answer is damage rather than a lock, which is slow going against inflated enemy pools, and the skill list is whatever the two of you happened to take at creation.

vars.note: Trades the free temp-HP tick for an oath that halves what lands on you outright, with everything then queueing behind a single Channel Oath charge.
Buys the heavy front and the maximised burst the monk cannot supply, and gives up the rest-free buff.

vars.text: Skill split: whichever partner you take, settle the proficiency list at creation — neither body can Expertise its way out of a gate later.

Lunar.name: Lunar & Armament
Lunar.verdict: Reads as. Every defensive line the oath owns points at the other body — halved incoming damage on the partner, an aura subtracting Charisma from every hit either takes — and Armament is the rare carry that needs none of the oath's slots to function. Will Over Weave answers the enemy caster without spending anything the oath was saving for itself.
Lunar.cost: Costs. The halving, the blind and the slow all draw on the same Channel Oath charge, so no fight gets more than one of them. Two Charisma bodies compete for the same gear and the same dialogue role, and between them they bring no skill list worth the name and nothing that moves quickly.

vars.note: Layers physical resistance and a reroll-forcing rune under the aura, trading the partner's single-stat simplicity for a second body that cannot reposition.
Swaps the Charisma twin for a Wisdom one, so the pair stops fighting over gear and gains a mobile flank.

vars.text: Charge discipline: Divine Guardian and Full Moon want the same resource — decide before initiative which kind of fight this is.

Plate.name: Plate & Lunar
Plate.verdict: Reads as. The hardest two bodies on the list to actually put down: the oath halves what lands on the artificer, Guardian rips the attacker off the paladin, and Lone Wolf's spare reaction means that pull is never the reaction you needed for something else. Arcane Armor supplies its own heavy armour, so the Fighter levels are bought purely for Action Surge and cost nothing.
Plate.cost: Costs. Nothing here ends an encounter quickly — the pair grinds fights down, which means standing through a great many enemy turns to do it. Intelligence and Charisma split the party's coverage across two lists that barely overlap, and the fuel is long-rest on the half that matters.

vars.note: Adds a genuine skill list and a Charisma face, at the cost of the oath's damage halving.
Replaces the aura with a rest-free buff and hands the pair a second mobile body, softening the front considerably.

vars.text: Reaction budget: the second reaction is what makes Guardian free — do not spend it on an opportunity attack.

Breath.name: Breath & Kinship
Breath.verdict: Reads as. Two Wisdom bodies sitting at the same ceiling, which is exactly what makes the bond's temp-HP tick land at full value on both halves rather than at the weaker one's rate. The breath replaces an attack instead of costing a bonus action, so both of Lone Wolf's Actions carry a cone, and the Wyrm's resistance layers on top of the blessing's.
Breath.cost: Costs. Two monks between them clear almost nothing outside combat — this is the thinnest coverage on the list, and named checks will simply fail. No armour, no revive, no heal, and no answer at all to a problem that is not a creature.

vars.note: Buys the entire out-of-combat list this pairing lacks, and gives up the matched Wisdom floor that keeps both bodies standing.
Trades the second monk for armour and an aura, and the pair loses its mobility in the exchange.

vars.text: Damage type: choose the breath's element against the endgame's resistances, not against what the early acts are made of.

Sigil.name: Sigil & Lunar
Sigil.verdict: Reads as. Mitigation stacked in layers that do not overlap each other: physical resistance under a shield, a rune forcing a reroll on the hit aimed at the partner, an aura shaving every incoming attack, then the oath halving what survives all of that. Almost the whole toolbox is short-rest, so the last fight before camp looks much like the first.
Sigil.cost: Costs. Two static bodies with nothing that repositions — moving is a turn spent, and ranged enemies get precisely the fight they want. The pair kills slowly, and past one quietly useful Sleight of Hand the out-of-combat list is a fighter's and stays a fighter's.

vars.note: Puts an at-will ranged answer beside the rune wall, in exchange for a partner far easier to knock over.
Turns the pair's spare Actions into extra free swings, and drops the ranged coverage entirely.

vars.text: Sleight of Hand: on a Fighter it looks like a rounding error, but it is the only pickpocket key either body carries.

Flourish.name: Flourish & Kinship
Flourish.tag: flourishing sword bard + monk bond support
Flourish.verdict: Reads as. The bond covers exactly the hole the College leaves open: medium armour with no shield gets the blessing's AC and resistances at no action cost, and the free tick means reactions stay free for Goon's interrupt Flourishes instead of being spent on staying upright. Bard proficiencies give this pair a real out-of-combat list, which almost no monk pairing has.
Flourish.cost: Costs. The weapon wants Dexterity and the spell DC wants Charisma, so one of the two is permanently a step behind whatever the encounter asked for. Nothing here halves damage, nothing revives, and the pair's durability floor is set by whichever body is softer — which is the bard, always.

vars.note: Turns the pair into the widest skill list obtainable, and gives up what little front line it had.
Puts shields and martial weapons on the other side, so the fragile half stops being both halves.

Pyre.name: Pyre & Kinship
Pyre.verdict: Reads as. The one bond pairing with a genuine crowd answer — a maximised Fireball twice a short rest, on a body that has been swinging as a bonus action since level one. Both halves run on Wisdom, so the tick and the blessing land at their ceiling on each, and heavy armour finally gives a monk-bond pair something like a hard front.
Pyre.cost: Costs. Revivify and Death Ward arrive an entire act later than the split implies, so the early game has no safety net whatsoever. Out of combat the pair is very close to blank, and a static armoured body beside a mobile one means the two are rarely where each other's auras and ticks are useful.

vars.note: Adds the control and the skill coverage this pairing has none of, at the cost of the matched Wisdom durability floor.
Swaps the free buff for a partner that needs no fuel at all, leaving the Cleric's slots entirely to the Cleric.

vars.text: Act I: with no revive until the Cleric half matures, play the opening act as a party that cannot be picked back up — because it cannot.

Anthem.name: Anthem & Kinship
Anthem.verdict: Reads as. The bond takes the party-buff duty off the bard completely, which frees Anthem's own concentration for control — the pair holds exactly two concentration slots and this is one of the few pairings that spends them on different jobs. Shields and martial weapons from the College itself mean the buff body is also a real swing body.
Anthem.cost: Costs. Improved Extra Attack never arrives, so the swing count freezes at precisely the point the game's own ceiling starts climbing. A static bard beside a mobile monk drifts apart in practice, and everything the bard cannot reach has to be reached by the monk, which is not much.

vars.note: Replaces the free buff with extra bodies on the field and a far wider proficiency list.
Puts an at-will ranged answer opposite the shield, and then both halves are drinking from one ability score.

Aria.name: Aria & Peerless
Aria.verdict: Reads as. Every named gate in the run opens, and one Action buys a whole fight's worth of control — a stun landing on everything still Electrified, off a track that sharpens each turn instead of decaying. Magical Secrets brings Haste and Revivify years ahead of schedule, which is the only reason a pair this soft is playable at all.
Aria.cost: Costs. Light armour on both halves and no hard front anywhere; the durability floor is set low at creation and never moves. Lightning and thunder are the two types the endgame most reliably resists, and the fuel is long-rest, so a third fight before camp is a genuine question rather than a formality.

vars.note: Buys the heavy front and the damage halving the two-bard version simply does not have, giving up roughly half the skill list.
Doubles down on lightning and adds Twinned Haste, which makes the resisted-type problem worse rather than better.

vars.text: Revivify: bought early through Magical Secrets, it is what keeps this pair upright — keep the diamonds stocked.

Infernal.name: Infernal & Anthem
Infernal.verdict: Reads as. Two Charisma bodies both running on short-rest fuel, so the pair's whole day resets at a campfire rather than a bedroll. Agonizing Blast never runs dry, and the fiend's luck, temp HP and resilience are exactly what a bard in shields still needs on the turns it turns out to be the tougher of the two.
Infernal.cost: Costs. Eldritch Cone stops scaling after the middle act, so the area damage that carried the pair falls away and nothing in either progression replaces it. Neither body brings a heavy front or a real rescue, and both fish from the same Charisma pool for every item worth wearing.

vars.note: Trades the second Charisma body for heavy armour and a maximised burst, and the pair stops competing for gear.
Moves the weapon half onto Intelligence, which splits the gear demand but also splits the dialogue coverage.

vars.text: Act III: once the cone flattens, area damage has to come from gear or scrolls — buy it before the act that needs it.

Pactblade.name: Pactblade & Kinship
Pactblade.tag: pact-weapon warlock melee + monk bond support
Pactblade.verdict: Reads as. The bond is the only thing in this pair pointed at anyone but its owner — Pactblade aims every feature at itself, so all of the partner-facing text comes from the monk's side. Both halves refuel on short rests, which is why the day stretches further here than the swing count on its own suggests.
Pactblade.cost: Costs. The Spellblade dip stops well short of the feature the plan is named after, so those levels buy a stat conversion and very little else. Nothing halves damage, nothing revives, and the crowd answer is whatever the pact slots can be talked into sparing.

vars.note: Finally puts something partner-facing on the other side of the pair, at the price of the rest-free tick.
Keeps the short-rest rhythm and adds a repeatable cone, but then neither body does anything at all for the other.

Pirouette.name: Pirouette & Lunar
Pirouette.verdict: Reads as. A fragile body propped up by the most partner-facing oath in the game: the aura shaves every incoming hit and the halving covers the turns the dancer is standing somewhere it has no business standing. Inspiring the paladin is free damage as well, since every inspiration die throws a kick along with it.
Pirouette.cost: Costs. Extra Attack never arrives, so the whole build's output rides riders on a swing count that never grows. The unarmoured AC wants a third ability score on top of the two the chassis already needs, so nothing ends up where it should be — and the oath's kit is still competing for one charge.

vars.note: A College that actually reaches Extra Attack on the other side, which is the swing count this body cannot buy for itself.
Trades the armoured front for every gate in the run, on a pair that was already short on durability.

Umbra.name: Umbra & Kinship
Umbra.verdict: Reads as. The scouting a two-body party has no room to spare for, bought off the ki pool rather than a slot — Hide, party-wide Pass Without Trace, Shadow Step. Rogue levels supply the Expertise that monk pairings otherwise go without, and the bond's temp HP is what makes standing behind the enemy line something you survive.
Umbra.cost: Costs. A great many small hits and no burst at all, so this pair takes longer to close an encounter than anything ranked above it. Neither half wears armour, neither can pick the other up, and the Rogue opening pushes the deep Monk features back a level band.

vars.note: Adds the bonus-action heal and the revive this pairing has no route to, at the cost of the matched melee floor.
Buys slot-free area charm-or-fear from level one, which is the crowd control a flurry of small hits never provides.

vars.text: Rogue first: the level-one opening is what buys the skills — taken later it costs the extra proficiencies outright.

Bombard.name: Bombard & Anthem
Bombard.verdict: Reads as. One character fielding several bodies: cannons that resummon off a companion template rather than a daily charge, plus a homunculus, so the action economy on the field is much wider than the head count implies. The bard holds the line while the artillery works, and between the two the proficiency coverage is genuinely broad.
Bombard.cost: Costs. Setup is the tax — the emplacement has to be placed and replaced, and a fight that resolves before it matters is a fight fought with half a build. Neither body is hard to kill, and the bard's swing count stops climbing well before the endgame does.

vars.note: Puts a real melee body and a Charisma face beside the artillery, in exchange for the bard's buff coverage.
Adds slot-free area control from level one, so the cannons fire into a crowd that is already pinned.

vars.text: Placement: the emplacement is the build — entering a fight without a turn to set up is entering it at half strength.

Stormvest.name: Stormvest & Lunar
Stormvest.verdict: Reads as. Twinned Haste on both bodies is the largest single tempo swing any pairing here can produce, and the one-level dip means the sorcerer is wearing heavy armour and a shield while producing it. The oath's halving is what keeps that concentration standing once the enemy works out where it came from.
Stormvest.cost: Costs. Long-rest slots and a shallow sorcery-point pool on one side, an oath wanting its charge back on the other — this pair empties faster than anything else on the list, and the last fight before camp is visibly worse than the first. Lightning is also a resisted type precisely where the maximising matters most.

vars.note: Swaps the armoured partner for control that outlasts the sorcerer's slots, which does nothing whatever for the fuel problem.
Adds a rest-free buff and a tougher second body — the closest this chassis comes to fixing its supply.

vars.text: Camp cost: this pair long-rests more often than any other here; budget supplies for it from the first act.

Panache.name: Panache & Lunar
Panache.verdict: Reads as. Damage subtracted three separate times before it lands: the Parry stance takes a die and both modifiers off the hit, the aura shaves it again, and the oath halves whatever survives. Charisma on unarmoured AC means the defence rides the same score the oath is already maximising, so nothing is being paid for twice.
Panache.cost: Costs. Extra Attack and the third reaction are both leashed to holding Panache, which outside crits and kills with the right weapon only returns on a long rest — the offensive half of the chassis is switched off more often than on. This is the slowest pair on the list at removing anything from the field.

vars.note: Adds AC and a free cushion on top of the Parry stance, giving up the oath's halving and its armoured front.

vars.text: Weapon choice: a one-handed piercing weapon is not a preference here — without it Panache never returns mid-fight and half the chassis stays dark.

cards.title: Coverage is derived, not chosen
cards.body: The roster is not a shortlist somebody liked. Every ### heading in the seventeen class files was enumerated mechanically — 157 of them — and each one had to come back with a verdict. 146 seeded at least one viable twenty-level body; eleven were rejected in writing, and those rejections are listed under Caveats rather than deleted. A subclass that is missing from this ledger is missing because someone wrote down why.

cards.title: A subclass is not one chassis
cards.body: The unit of scoring is the build, not the subclass. A Hexblade is a Charisma smite frontliner and a short-rest blaster; those are different bodies that want different partners, and collapsing them to one loses whichever was not written down. Seeds therefore carry builds keyed by niche, capped at three — past three you are reflavouring one of the first three. 146 candidates produced 150 builds.

cards.title: Everything viable was scored
cards.body: No triage cut was applied before scoring. The sweep produced a coarse peak estimate per build purely to make rationing possible if the budget would not stretch; it did, so peak was discarded and all 150 builds were scored in full. Selection happens downstream on real pair numbers, which are strictly better information than the estimate that existed only to make the sweep cheap.

cards.title: Ten axes, three acts, four blocks
cards.body: Each body carries ten axis values per act against a written rubric, with Act I at characters 3–8, II at 9–15 and III at 16–20. Rungs are act-relative: a 5 in Act I means as good as a body can be at character 8, not as good as a body ever gets. The four blocks — Tempo, Resilience, Duration, Utility — are the reporting surface; there is no single total, on purpose.

cards.title: Saves are evidence, not a number
cards.body: Index 8 of every score array is null. The saves axis is authored as the resulting proficiency set plus any blanket boosters, and derived at render time, because its rubric is written in terms of which abilities are covered and whether the grants are disjoint. A bare 0–5 there could not be re-checked from outside; a proficiency set can.

cards.title: Every pair, then the frontier
cards.body: There is no carry/support partition. All 150 chassis are paired with all others — 11,175 unordered pairings — and the entries are the Pareto frontier over the four blocks: 187 pairings that nothing else beats on all four at once. 47 chassis appear somewhere on that frontier. Everything else stays in the field table as the audit trail, dominated rather than deleted.

cards.title: Nothing quoted is hand-written
cards.body: Every figure in this document — scores, block percentages, utilisation, variation lines — is computed at render time from about 1,500 authored integers. The previous ledger's largest source of error was hand-copied numbers going stale after a re-score; here they cannot, because they do not exist until the page is built.

caveats.h2: What this ledger does not know

excluded.summary: Rejected in the sweep, and why
items: Inquisitor (Tactics, Vengeance, Zeal) — subclasses are chosen at level 3 and the shipped install has a dangling subclass GUID there. Unusable past level 2 until the mod is updated to 2.2.1.
Sorcerer / Wretched Soul — no published feature list, levels or progression. Added to the list for testing.
Wizard / School of Bombardment — the mod page publishes its feature table only as images; nothing verifiable to build on.
Paladin / Oath of Illumination — nothing published beyond Aura of Brilliance; shipped for testing.
Druid / Circle of Dreams — only the level 14 feature is documented for this pack, and the author calls it wholly different from the published subclass.
Barbarian / Path of the Battlerager — flat 1d4 spikes and 3-point retaliation never scale against Combat Extender's HP, and medium metal armour forfeits Unarmoured Defence.
Monk / Way of the Four Elements (vanilla) — folded into Warrior of the Elements, which the class file states supersedes it in almost every respect.
Cleric's heavy-armour table and Paladin's Oath Framework library parse as headings but are not subclasses — a comparison table and a modder API respectively.
excluded.lead: Eleven of 157 headings produced no chassis. They are listed so that a gap in coverage is legible as a decision rather than an oversight.

settled.summary: Settled by reading the installed paks
items: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 per beam in this list, not 1d10. Any damage arithmetic imported from outside Listo is overstated.
Eldritch Cone and Line stop scaling at character 10 — LevelMapValue(EldritchZoneDamage) ends at 3d10 — and the cone's success roll never checks Agonizing Blast.
Combat Extender is at +126% regular and +170% boss HP, which is what makes a flat, non-upcasting feature fall across the acts rather than merely stand still.
Absolute Wrath is on, so ordinary enemies carry layered resistances. A body locked to one commonly-resisted damage type caps at 4 on single-target from Act II.
Save DCs decay against the curve: bosses gain +1 spell save DC per 7 levels, ordinary enemies +1 per 11. Pure save-DC control loses a rung by Act III; imposing disadvantage on the save does not.
Feats land at character 3/6/9/12/13/15/18, plus 11 for Fighter and Rogue. Every individual mod page's own feat table is wrong for this list.

assumptions.summary: Assumptions that would still move numbers
items: The booster registry is short, and that under-counts saves. Only three blanket save effects have ids — Brutish Durability, War Caster and Aura of Protection. At least ten scored chassis have a real blanket save effect with no id, so it contributes nothing and they render a rung low on the heaviest-weighted axis in the Resilience block. The two chassis that lead the frontier as partners, Kinship (Friar's Blessing, +1d4 to all saves on both bodies) and Lunar (Lunar Champion, Charisma to all saves in an aura), are both affected, as are Peace's Emboldening Bond, Spellblade's Magic Resistance, Rune Knight's Frost Rune, Mesmerist's Towering Ego and Blood Hunter's Dark Augmentation. The error is one-directional — these bodies are too low, never too high — but it is large enough to reorder the frontier if the ids were added.

Frontier membership inherits the provisional weights. Dominance over four blocks is ordinal and fairly robust, but the Resilience block's internal weighting — saves at 3.0 down to rescue at 1.5 — does decide which pairings survive. Change those and the 187 changes.

Scores rise across the acts far more than they fall. Across 150 chassis, 883 axis values rise from Act I to Act III and only 34 fall. Rungs are supposed to be act-relative, which should make movement roughly symmetric; a 26:1 ratio says the scoring drifted toward absolute capability. It compresses Act I and inflates late-game pairings relative to early ones.

Levelling order is not recorded. A split names one to three classes with their totals and nothing else. Which block is taken first frequently decides armour, save proficiencies and whether Extra Attack lands in Act I or Act II — several chassis note the assumption they were scored under. That decision belongs to a pair sheet, not to this ledger.

Splits are provisional. They came out of a sweep that read each subclass's own section plus every class's dip table, and were revisited but not re-derived during scoring. One seed premise was found false outright: Pactblade was seeded for slot-free Counterspell at Paragon 3, and that feature is Paragon 13.

Several chassis rest on sources that are not the installed pak. Stormcalling, Chronoknight and Circle of Wrath are documented only on their authors' sites; War Magic's feature table is images-only; the Lightning Vessel figures predate a nerf patch shipped inside the Wabbajack but absent from the manifest.

Two axes cannot express a self-inflicted risk. Lycan's Bloodlust and Wild Magic's surges can turn a body against its partner, which in a duo is half the party; both are scored neutral because no axis prices it. Revenant's inability to be healed by any means is the same shape — a pairing constraint, not an axis value.
